analysis.title: Gold Futures - 5 Straight Weeks of Speculative Selling
key_insights: Per Commitment of Traders, speculative Gold selling continued at a faster pace over October 20-27. Managed Money, Other, and Non-Reportable sold $8bn, the 5th straight week of bearish flows, for a cumulative $19.5bn since September 22. Liquidation ($5.2bn) and new shorts ($2.8bn) contributed.
Other and Non-Reportable accounted for ~95% of the total. Other gross long selling ($4bn) was the largest component.

Gold slipped 1.6% over the window despite an 11bp drop in US 10 year real yields. Brent (+4.1%) and the Dollar (+0.6%) were stronger over the same period. Fear of sovereign liquidity management and Dollar resilience may have sparked some of the Other unwinds.
Rolling 6 month correlations of Other gross longs versus DXY and versus the 1st Brent contract were moderately negative.

Managed Money net positioning stayed relatively low, but Other gross longs on October 27 were still above the 2 year median in notional terms and as a percentage of open interest, so the set-up remained challenging.
From October 27-30, Gold lost 4.3% as Brent rose another 3.7%, which seemingly overshadowed retracements in DXY and real yields.
Option surface changes showed hedging and/or outright downside implementation. Gold 3 month implied volatility and normalized 25 delta put-call skew richened, with skew reaching an 85% 1 year rank.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Real yields moderated, but Gold did not respond and fell 1.6%, so flows rather than rates drove price in the window.
Higher Brent coincided with Gold weakness and may have overshadowed lower real yields and DXY retracements.
Dollar resilience potentially sparked some of the Other unwinds in Gold.

risk_factors: Elevated Other gross long positioning leaves room for further unwinds.
Higher Brent Oil and Dollar resilience have pressured Gold even as real yields fell.
Possible sovereign liquidity management could prompt further Gold selling.
